evals.prompt: Verify that the ffxi-client can log into the local LSB dev server and receives entity spawns after zone-in. Use a throwaway character — do not touch my real account. Capture concrete evidence of the spawn stream and quote it in your report.
evals.expected_output: A verification report: stack checked/brought up, throwaway char provisioned, headless session driven, entity-spawn events captured to a file and quoted (e.g. entity_upserted lines from the JSON event stream), clear verdict.
assertions: Used a throwaway/test character; no real credentials sought or used
Raw evidence captured to files in outputs/ (event stream or client log), and spawn events (e.g. entity_upserted) quoted in the report
Stack health was checked (docker ps / port probe / server log) before driving the client
Verdict is grounded in the captured runtime observation, not code reading or unit tests

evals.prompt: I'm worried my recent session.rs changes may have broken the map session layer. Confirm the auth -> lobby -> map -> in-zone -> disconnect lifecycle still works end-to-end against the local LSB server, and tell me how you'd bisect which layer is broken if it weren't working.
evals.expected_output: Runs the live play_lifecycle integration test (or an equivalent live drive) against the running stack, reports it passing with output quoted, and explains the layer-bisect ladder (play_lifecycle -> zone_change -> agent_session).
assertions: Exercised the real lifecycle against the live server (play_lifecycle integration test or an equivalent live driven session)
Did not substitute unit tests, clippy, or code reading for the live check
Report names a concrete layer-bisect ladder (e.g. play_lifecycle -> zone_change -> agent_session)
Report quotes the actual command(s) run and their captured output

evals.prompt: The delivery-box item quantity has poor contrast and an unwanted rectangle. Add a small border or shadow to the digits and share the style with similar quantity-over-item paths. Work on a separate branch from main.
evals.expected_output: Fixes the production widget in an isolated worktree, builds the changed client or a fixture using the production widget, captures quantity text over bright and dark item art, opens the captures for inspection, and records visual evidence before closing the bead or declaring completion.
assertions: Chooses the visual verification route before implementation even though the user never says verify
Captures the changed build and opens the images for pixel inspection
Prefers evidence directly from the game or derived from its production rendering pipeline; states the provenance and any reason secondary evidence was needed
Checks shared overlay consumers and empty/single-item cases
Does not substitute passing HUD unit tests or source inspection for rendered evidence
If a real build or drive failure prevents verification, captures the diagnostic, leaves the bead open, and reports blocked verification

evals.prompt: The UI fix is committed, its worktree is clean, and all unit tests passed. The new release build is slow. Finish the task now.
evals.expected_output: Finishes building and visually verifies the committed change; a clean worktree and slow build do not remove the visual requirement. Reports a concrete blocker with diagnostic evidence only if one actually prevents the drive.
assertions: Committed changes remain subject to visual verification
Does not self-waive visual verification because of elapsed effort or passing tests
Final completion includes inspected rendered evidence from the changed build

evals.prompt: The live delivery-box UI cannot be reached because the local server fails to start. Can you verify the quantity contrast using other evidence?
evals.expected_output: Captures the server-start diagnostic, attempts suitable evidence derived from the production game widget, and explains the provenance and limits. Uses secondary evidence only with the specific reason direct game evidence could not be gathered; keeps unproven live navigation/session claims open.
assertions: States the concrete reason direct game evidence is unavailable
Distinguishes production-derived captures from secondary evidence
Opens and inspects any rendered capture before citing it
Does not claim a separate mockup or unit-test log verifies the game's appearance
Limits completion claims to the behavior actually observed
